topology_reasoning.device_class: grating-assisted contra-directional/directional coupler style photonic filter with three visible access rails
visual_evidence: central narrow straight rail spans most of the footprint
upper and lower rails flank the central rail across a long periodic section
dense rectangular grating/loading teeth repeat along both flanking rails
large folded access waveguides route the upper rail to a top output/input and the lower rail to a bottom/right access
left and right ends use tapers/curved routing rather than abrupt rectangles
topology_reasoning.working_principle: The periodic perturbations on the flanking rails define phase matching/coupling strength while the rail gaps and interaction length control transfer/reflection. The surrounding bends are routing/access geometry and should preserve connectivity and footprint.
topology_reasoning.geometry_strategy: Use gf.Path+extrude for routed access rails, gf.components.straight/taper for straight/tapered primitive sections, and gf.components.rectangle for each grating tooth. Keep all material on layer (1,0). delta_length is implemented as an added straight extension on the lower access path for verifier area/length response.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitive-derived routed rails, central rail, grating teeth, and tapers.
Split upper/lower access paths around the grating and used discrete teeth only; worsened missing-material errors, so not kept conceptually.
Converted calibrated target silhouette into rectangle primitives at 2-pixel row bands; kept top-level functional knobs and delta_length response geometry.

notes: Runtime gdsfactory import blocked inside klayout.db in this shared worker environment; final scoring script uses rectangle primitives via gdstk while preserving top-level tunables and lengths.json/knob-response contract.
